arxiv-1607-06433.title: Uniformization of embedded surfaces
arxiv-1607-06433.creator: N. P. Strickland
arxiv-1607-06433.description: Abstract 1. Introduction Let X\subset S^{3} be a smoothly embedded closed surface of genus g>1 . As we will explain, X automatically has a very rich and rigid geometric structure. Indeed, X inherits a Riemannian metric from S^{3} , and after specifying some conventions we also obtain a well-defined orientation.

arxiv-2004-05887.title: Frequency-Guided Word Substitutions for Detecting Textual Adversarial Examples
arxiv-2004-05887.creator: Maximilian Mozes, Pontus Stenetorp, Bennett Kleinberg, Lewis D. Griffin
arxiv-2004-05887.description: Abstract Recent efforts have shown that neural text processing models are vulnerable to adversarial examples, but the nature of these examples is poorly understood. In this work, we show that adversarial attacks against CNN, LSTM and Transformer-based classification models perform word substitutions that are identifiable through frequency differences between replaced words and their corresponding substitutions.

arxiv-2009-06425.title: Persistent And Scalable JADE: A Cloud based In Memory Multi-agent Framework
arxiv-2009-06425.creator: Nauman Khalid, Ghalib Tahir, Peter Bloodsworth
arxiv-2009-06425.description: Abstract Email: 11mscsnkhalid@seecs.edu.pk Email: 12mscsgtahir@seecs.edu.pk Email: peter.bloodsworth@cs.ox.ac.uk (Corresponding author) I 1. Abstract Multi-agent systems are often limited in terms of persistence and scalability. This issue is more prevalent for applications in which agent states changes frequently. This makes the existing methods less usable as they increase the agent’s complexity and are less scalable.

arxiv-2101-03302.title: Origin of Galactic Spurs: New Insight from Radio/X-ray All-sky Maps Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2101-03302.creator: Jun Kataoka, Marino Yamamoto, Yuki Nakamura, Soichiro Ito, Yoshiaki Sofue, Yoshiyuki Inoue, Takeshi Nakamori, Tomonori Totani
arxiv-2101-03302.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jun Kataoka, Marino Yamamoto, Yuki Nakamura, Soichiro Ito, Yoshiaki Sofue, Yoshiyuki Inoue, Takeshi Nakamori, Tomonori Totani. In this study, we analyze giant Galactic spurs seen in both radio and X-ray all-sky maps to reveal their origins.

arxiv-2102-02430.title: Reconfigurable-intelligent-surface-assisted Downlink Transmission Design via Bayesian Optimization
arxiv-2102-02430.creator: Dong Wang, Xiaodong Wang, Fanggang Wang
arxiv-2102-02430.description: Abstract This paper investigates the transmission design in the reconfigurable-intelligent-surface (RIS)-assisted downlink system. The channel state information (CSI) is usually difficult to be estimated at the base station (BS) when the RIS is not equipped with radio frequency chains. In this paper, we propose a downlink transmission framework with unknown CSI via Bayesian optimization.

arxiv-2103-04330.title: An Overview of Cryptographic Accumulators
arxiv-2103-04330.creator: Ilker Ozcelik 1,2 , Sai Medury 1 and Justin Broaddus 1 , Anthony Skjellum 1 1 SimCenter & Department of Computer Science and Engineering, University of Tennessee at Chattanooga, Chattanooga, Tennessee, USA 2 Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Rize, Turkey ozcelikilker@ieee.org, Sai-Medury@mocs.utc.edu, { Justin-
arxiv-2103-04330.description: Abstract This paper is a primer on cryptographic accumulators and how to apply them practically. A cryptographic accumulator is a space- and time-efficient data structure used for set-membership tests. Since it is possible to represent any computational problem where the answer is yes or no as a set-membership problem, cryptographic accumulators are invaluable data structures in computer science and engineering.

arxiv-2106-01282.title: Spectral embedding for dynamic networks with stability guarantees
arxiv-2106-01282.creator: Ian Gallagher, Andrew Jones, Patrick Rubin-Delanchy
arxiv-2106-01282.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ian Gallagher, Andrew Jones, Patrick Rubin-Delanchy. We consider the problem of embedding a dynamic network, to obtain time-evolving vector representations of each node, which can then be used to describe changes in behaviour of individual nodes, communities, or the entire graph.

arxiv-2210-09976.title: Phenomenological Model of Superconducting Optoelectronic Loop Neurons
arxiv-2210-09976.creator: Jeffrey M. Shainline ∗ , Bryce A. Primavera, and Saeed Khan National Institute of Standards and Technology 325 Broadway, Boulder, CO, USA, 80305 ∗ jeffrey.shainline@nist.gov
arxiv-2210-09976.description: Abstract Superconducting optoelectronic loop neurons are a class of circuits potentially conducive to networks for large-scale artificial cognition. These circuits employ superconducting components including single-photon detectors, Josephson junctions, and transformers to achieve neuromorphic functions. To date, all simulations of loop neurons have used first-principles circuit analysis to model the behavior of synapses, dendrites, and neurons.

arxiv-2302-10466.creator: Chengyuan Li (李程远), Xin Ji (纪鑫), Long Wang (王龙), Yue Wang (王悦), Baitian Tang (汤柏添), Antonino P. Milone, Yujiao Yang (杨玉姣), Holger Baumgardt, Dengkai Jiang (姜登凯)
arxiv-2302-10466.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Chengyuan Li (李程远), Xin Ji (纪鑫), Long Wang (王龙), Yue Wang (王悦), Baitian Tang (汤柏添), Antonino P. Milone, Yujiao Yang (杨玉姣), Holger Baumgardt, Dengkai Jiang (姜登凯). Helium variations are common features of globular clusters (GCs) with multiple stellar populations. All the formation scenarios predict that secondary population stars are enhanced in helium but the exact helium content depends on the polluters.

arxiv-2306-03192.title: Anomalous coupling in radiation mediated shocks
arxiv-2306-03192.creator: Amir Levinson \aff 1 \corresp, Alon Granot \aff 1, Arno Vanthieghem \aff 2,3, Jens Mahlmann \aff 3
arxiv-2306-03192.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Amir Levinson \aff 1 \corresp, Alon Granot \aff 1, Arno Vanthieghem \aff 2,3, Jens Mahlmann \aff 3. We summarize recent attempts to unravel the role of plasma kinetic effects in radiation mediated shocks. Such shocks form in all strong stellar explosions and are responsible for the early electromagnetic emission released from these events.

arxiv-2311-17179.title: SatCLIP: Global, General-Purpose Location Embeddings with Satellite Imagery
arxiv-2311-17179.creator: Konstantin Klemmer, Esther Rolf, Caleb Robinson, Lester Mackey, Marc Rußwurm
arxiv-2311-17179.description: Abstract Geographic location is essential for modeling tasks in fields ranging from ecology to epidemiology to the Earth system sciences. However, extracting relevant and meaningful characteristics of a location can be challenging, often entailing expensive data fusion or data distillation from global imagery datasets.

arxiv-2312-05658.title: Monoid Theory in Alonzo A Little Theories Formalization in Simple Type Theory
arxiv-2312-05658.creator: William M. Farmer, Dennis Y. Zvigelsky
arxiv-2312-05658.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by William M. Farmer, Dennis Y. Zvigelsky. Alonzo is a practice-oriented classical higher-order logic that extends first-order logic and that admits undefined expressions. Named in honor of Alonzo Church, Alonzo is based on Church’s type theory, Church’s formulation of simple type theory. The little theories method is a method for formalizing mathematical knowledge as a theory graph consisting of theories as nodes and theory morphisms as directed edges.

arxiv-2405-10978.title: Some notes on an identity of Frisch
arxiv-2405-10978.description: Abstract In this note, we show how a combinatorial identity of Frisch can be applied to prove and generalize some well-known identities involving harmonic numbers. We also present some combinatorial identities involving odd harmonic numbers which can be inferred straightforwardly from our results. Kunle Adegoke Department of Physics and Engineering Physics Obafemi Awolowo University, 220005 Ile-Ife, Nigeria adegoke00@gmail.

arxiv-2410-06845.title: MentalArena: Self-play Training of Language Models for Diagnosis and Treatment of Mental Health Disorders
arxiv-2410-06845.creator: Cheng Li, May Fung, Qingyun Wang, Chi Han, Manling Li, Jindong Wang, Heng Ji
arxiv-2410-06845.description: Abstract Mental health disorders are one of the most serious diseases in the world. Most people with such a disease lack access to adequate care, which highlights the importance of training models for the diagnosis and treatment of mental health disorders.

arxiv-2412-17139.title: Style Transfer Dataset: What Makes A Good Stylization?
arxiv-2412-17139.creator: Victor Kitov, Valentin Abramov, Mikhail Akhtyrchenko
arxiv-2412-17139.description: Abstract We present a new dataset with the goal of advancing image style transfer - the task of rendering one image in the style of another image. The dataset covers various content and style images of different size and contains 10.000 stylizations manually rated by three annotators in 1-10 scale.

arxiv-2503-02181.title: Supernova remnant candidates identified using MWA Galactic Plane Monitoring over 285 ∘ < l < 70 ∘ 285^{\circ}<l<70^{\circ} and | b | < 16 ∘ |b|<16^{\circ}
arxiv-2503-02181.creator: S. Mantovanini, N. Hurley-Walker, G. E. Anderson
arxiv-2503-02181.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by S. Mantovanini, N. Hurley-Walker, G. E. Anderson. Observations of Galactic supernova remnants (SNRs) are crucial to understanding supernova explosion mechanisms and their impact on our Galaxy’s evolution. SNRs are usually identified by searching for extended, circular structures in all-sky surveys. However, the resolution and sensitivity of any given survey results in selection biases related to the brightness and angular scale of a subset of the total SNR population.

arxiv-2508-06872.title: Perceiving Slope and Acceleration: Evidence for Variable Tempo Sampling in Pitch-Based Sonification of Functions
arxiv-2508-06872.creator: \authororcid Danyang Fan0000-0002-3368-7887 \authororcid Walker Smith0009-0000-5850-4728 \authororcid Takako Fujioka0000-0003-2421-9106 \authororcid Chris Chafe0000-0002-5381-0109 \authororcid Sile O’Modhrain0000-0003-3804-5469 \authororcid Diana Deutsch0000-0002-6060-1196 \authororcid Sean Follmer0
arxiv-2508-06872.description: Abstract Sonification offers a non-visual way to understand data, with pitch-based encodings being the most common. Yet, how well people perceive slope and acceleration—key features of data trends—remains poorly understood. Drawing on people’s natural abilities to perceive tempo, we introduce a novel sampling method for pitch-based sonification to enhance the perception of slope and acceleration in univariate functions.

Morley, Sagnick Mukherjee, Jonathan J. Fortney, Peter Gao, Nikole K. Lewis, L. C. Mayorga, Logan A. Pearce, Hannah R. Wakeford
arxiv-2508-15102.description: Abstract Here we present an open-source cloud model for substellar atmospheres, called Virga . The Virga-v0 series has already been widely adopted in the literature. It is written in Python and has heritage from the A. S. Ackerman & M. S. Marley 2001 model (often referred to as eddysed ), used to study clouds on both exoplanets and brown dwarfs.

arxiv-2509-08071.title: Tensor-Train Operator Inference
arxiv-2509-08071.creator: Engin Danis, and Duc Truong and Kim Ø. Rasmussen and Boian S. Alexandrov
arxiv-2509-08071.description: Abstract In this study, we present a tensor-train framework for nonintrusive operator inference aimed at learning discrete operators and using them to predict solutions of physical governing equations. Our framework comprises three approaches: full-order tensor-train operator inference, full-order quantized tensor-train operator inference, and reduced-order tensor-train operator inference.

pmc-11302921.title: Topography and soil variables drive the plant community distribution pattern and species richness in the Arjo-Diga forest in western Ethiopia
pmc-11302921.creator: Tariku Berihun Tenaw, Tamrat Bekele Gode, Ermias Lulekal Molla, Zemede Asfaw Woldemariam, Bhoj K. Acharya, Bhoj K. Acharya, Bhoj K. Acharya, Bhoj K. Acharya, Bhoj K. Acharya, Bhoj K. Acharya, Bhoj K. Acharya
pmc-11302921.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Understanding plant community characteristics, distributions, and environmental relationships is crucial for sustainable forest management. Thus, this study examined the relationships between plant community composition and topographic and soil variables within the Arjo-Diga forest. Vegetation data were collected from 72 nested plots (30 × 30 m2 and 2 × 2 m2) systematically laid along nine transects spaced 300 to 700 m apart. Environmental variables, including soil properties and anthropogenic disturbance, were recorded within each main plot.

pmc-11486274.title: COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy and intentions among parents of children with mental and behavioral disorders
pmc-11486274.creator: Mohamed Adil Shah Khoodoruth, Sami Ouanes, Kristian Somintac, Shaima Gulistan, Asieh Dehwari, Widaad Nuzhah Chut-Kai Khoodoruth, Mohammed Nasser Alamri, Majid Alabdulla, Yasser Saeed Khan
pmc-11486274.description: Parent vaccine hesitancy (PVH) remains a significant public health concern, particularly emphasized during the COVID-19 pandemic. This study investigates PVH among parents of children with various psychiatric and neurodevelopmental conditions, such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety disorders, and behavioral disturbances, extending previous research focused on autism spectrum disorder (ASD).

pmc-11539451.title: Construction of multilayered gene circuits using de-novo-designed synthetic transcriptional regulators in cell-free systems
pmc-11539451.creator: Mingming Zhao, Jeongwon Kim, Jiayan Jiao, Yelin Lim, Xianai Shi, Shaobin Guo, Jongmin Kim
pmc-11539451.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundDe-novo-designed synthetic transcriptional regulators have great potential as the genetic parts for constructing complex multilayered gene circuits. The design flexibility afforded by advanced nucleic acid sequence design tools vastly expands the repertoire of regulatory elements for circuit design.

pmc-12715892.title: Optimizing Computed Tomography (CT) for Structurally Complex Organisms: A Case Study of Gastropod Shell Features
pmc-12715892.creator: Andreza Caroline Caiero, Marilia Nagata Ragagnin, Cláudio Campi de Castro, Marcelo Gusmão Paraíso Cavalcanti, Daniel Gorman, Alexander Turra
pmc-12715892.description: The internal volume of gastropod shells is a measured metric in studies of hermit crab ecology, as it determines shell adequacy and subjective value. In this study, we developed and tested an optimized computed tomography (OCT) protocol to estimate shell volume as an alternative to traditional methods, using water or sand.

pmc-12966632.title: Differential Effects of Twice vs. Four Times Weekly Combined Exercise Training in Aging Adults With Hypertension: A Randomized Clinical Trial
pmc-12966632.creator: Rodrigo Ferrari, Vinícius Mallmann Schneider, Lucas Betti Domingues, Rodrigo Abreu, Gabriel Lemes, Rodrigo Leal‐Menezes, Hirofumi Tanaka, Sandra Costa Fuchs, Leandro de Oliveira Carpes
pmc-12966632.description: Current exercise guidelines emphasize a total weekly volume of exercise (i.e., 150 min/week), but the optimal weekly frequency remains uncertain. Therefore, this randomized clinical trial aimed to compare the effects of combined resistance and aerobic training either two or four times per week, at the same total weekly volume, on office and ambulatory blood pressure in older adults with hypertension.

pmc-13271764.title: Use of passive integrated transponder tags to assess movements and demography of Townsend’s Big-eared Bat (Corynorhinus townsendii) in Colorado
pmc-13271764.creator: Daniel J Neubaum, Jeremy L Siemers, Phillip Nyland, Kellen M Keisling, Terutaka Funabashi, Burton Lim
pmc-13271764.description: Determining bat seasonal roost use, demographic rates (fidelity and survival), and movements are necessary metrics to rigorously evaluate population status and trends. Little is known about these metrics for Townsend’s big-eared bats (Corynorhinus townsendii), a state and federal sensitive species, in Colorado.

pmc-13276336.title: LViM: Language-Infused Visual Mamba for apple leaf pests and diseases precise segmentation in complex environments
pmc-13276336.creator: Jiale Chen, Wei Shi, Ziyang Shi, Lin Li, Hao Zhou, Xuanhao Li
pmc-13276336.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Apple leaf disease segmentation is critical for yield and quality preservation in what is globally one of the most economically significant fruit crops. Despite recent advances in deep learning, real-world orchard environments present three primary challenges: (1) low contrast between lesions and background textures, which hinders accurate localization; (2) leaf overlap and occlusion, leading to incomplete feature representation and increased false negatives; and (3) the inherent limitations of unimodal RGB imagery in capturing subtle pathological features, which constrains generalization and accuracy.

pmc-13475436.title: Comparison of Ciprofol and Propofol on Postoperative Quality of Recovery and Intraoperative Cerebral Oxygen Saturation in Patients Undergoing Thoracoscopic Thoracic Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Non-Inferiority Trial
pmc-13475436.creator: Lideng Guo, Lianjie Cai, Botong Ni, Shiqi Shi, Chanjuan Huang, HaiFeng Lai, Quanchu Li, Ping Mo
pmc-13475436.description: PurposeCiprofol provides more stable induction, though its impact on patients’ quality of recovery (QoR) and brain oxygenation requires clarification. This trial assessed whether propofol anesthesia is non-inferior to ciprofol regarding postoperative recovery quality, while additionally comparing their effects on intraoperative cerebral oxygenation.

pmc-13583492.title: Advancing human sensorimotor research through modular robotics: the case of the HRX-1
pmc-13583492.creator: Ildar Farkhatdinov, Joshua Brown, Aaron Yurkewich, Etienne Burdet
pmc-13583492.description: The HRX-1 is a single-degree-of-freedom, direct-drive, modular and reconfigurable robotic device designed for investigating human sensorimotor control. By examining its use, this case study highlights the opportunities offered by modular, portable and user-centred open-source design approaches for sensorimotor diagnostics and basic neuromechanics research.

pmc-13645631.title: Neural pattern stability within events is similar in young and older adults
pmc-13645631.creator: Mohsen Davoudkhani, Michael Tollefsrud, Heather Bailey
pmc-13645631.description: Understanding how the brain segments continuous experiences into discrete events is essential for uncovering the mechanisms of episodic memory. Here, we investigated whether stable neural representations are maintained within unfolding events, how these representations differ between young and older adults, and whether they predict later memory.
